name: Tibni
overview: Tibni was a male figure in Israelite history noted for being a significant contender for the throne, as half of Israel supported him to be king. The Scriptures do not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details beyond his contested claim to kingship.
namesAndTitles: The name Tibni appears in Scripture without a provided meaning or divine origin. It is recorded simply as a proper name in 1 Kings 16:21, with no further explanation of its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Tibni is identified as the son of Ginath according to 1 Kings 16:21. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any additional family connections for Tibni.
scriptureSignificance: Tibni's significance lies in his role as a rival claimant to the throne of Israel, representing a faction that opposed the reigning king. His support by half of the nation highlights a period of division and contest for leadership within Israel. This episode underscores the challenges of maintaining unity and divine order in Israel's monarchy.
